scenes.narration: DarkCall is a sealed-bid auction on Zcash where no bid is ever opened, yet the price is proven and paid out in one shielded transaction.
Normally, checking the price means someone reads the bids: everyone after the close, or whoever makes the proof. And a proven price doesn't prove the payout.
Let's run one, live. A seller lists three units.

Each bidder's client splits its bid into three secret shares, one per operator, and proves in zero knowledge that they match its commitment. Operators check the proof and sign a receipt, but none can read a bid.
scenes.band: Each bid becomes three secret shares and a zero-knowledge proof
Bidding stays open until its deadline

scenes.narration: At the deadline, the operators certify the book. All three clear it on the shares with REP3, and coNoir turns that into one proof of the price, in about eight seconds. Nobody rebuilds a bid, not even the prover.
scenes.band: REP3 clears on the shares · coNoir proves the price

scenes.narration: Twenty-one per unit, three sold. Each bidder opens only its own result.
scenes.band: Each bidder opens only its own result

scenes.narration: That run had no deposits. On October 19th the same four bids ran on public Zcash testnet: shielded deposits into a two-of-three FROST escrow, six Halo2 proofs binding every payout to the result, and one shielded transaction.
scenes.band: 2-of-3 FROST escrow · six Halo2 payout proofs · one shielded transaction

scenes.narration: Here is that settlement. Bidder one decrypts its own receipt: one unit, at twenty-one. Everyone else sees one shielded transaction.
scenes.band: Each bidder decrypts only its own receipt

scenes.narration: Bidder four: no unit, full refund.
scenes.band: Each bidder decrypts only its own receipt

scenes.narration: Anyone can re-verify it with no secrets: the price proof, six payout proofs, the signed book and the Zcash signatures.
scenes.band: Public verification · no viewing key, no bid
